questions.text:
QUESTION ONE: CIRCULAR AND ROTATIONAL MOTION

A solid glass marble with a radius of 8.00 mm and a mass of 13.5 g is released from different heights on a curved plastic track. It rolls down and then travels over a series of humps. Each hump and dip has a radius of 40.0 mm.

In one trial, the marble reaches the bottom of the first dip with a velocity of 0.920 m s-1.

Calculate the angular velocity of the marble at the bottom of the first dip (Point X).
questions.expectedAnswer: v = r omega. 0.920 = 0.008 x omega. omega = 115 rad s-1.

questions.text:
Show that the maximum speed is 0.626 m s-1 in order for the marble to remain in contact with the track while going over the hump, at Point Y.

The hump has a radius of 40.0 mm.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- F_N = 0 at max speed.

For Merit:
- v = 0.626 m s-1.

questions.text:
Compare the forces acting at the top (Point Y) and bottom (Point X) of each hump, and explain how the net force varies.

Labelled force diagrams will be useful.
questions.expectedAnswer: At X (bottom): Fg down, FN up. FN > Fg so net force = FN - Fg = Fc (directed upward toward centre). At Y (top): Fg down, FN down (if any). Fc = Fg - FN (directed downward toward centre). At the top, the weight must provide the centripetal force.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- ONE correct statement.

For Merit:
- One position explained.

For Excellence:
- Full answer with both positions.

questions.text:
By considering energy changes, calculate the maximum height h above the top of the first hump (Point Y) that the marble can be released from if it is to remain in contact with the track.

The marble is a solid sphere with I = (2/5)mr^2.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Attempts energy conservation.

For Merit:
- Two energy terms correct.

For Excellence:
- h = 0.0280 m.

questions.text:
QUESTION TWO: ROTATIONAL MOTION

A tennis ball of mass 0.0580 kg is placed into a light cup attached to a flywheel, diameter 0.240 m, and accelerates downward at a constant rate of 1.95 m s-2.

Show that the angular acceleration of the flywheel is 16.25 rad s-2.
questions.expectedAnswer: a = r alpha. 1.95 = 0.12 x alpha. alpha = 16.25 rad s-2.

questions.text: If the ball and cup start from rest and fall through a distance of 0.850 m, calculate the final angular velocity of the flywheel.
questions.expectedAnswer: theta = d/r = 0.850/0.12 = 7.083 rad. omega_f^2 = omega_i^2 + 2 alpha theta = 0 + 2(16.25)(7.083) = 230.2. omega_f = 15.2 rad s-1.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Correct theta.

For Merit:
- Correct omega_f.

questions.text:
Calculate the rotational inertia of the flywheel.

Begin by calculating the force causing the flywheel to accelerate. A free-body diagram may assist.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Tension identified.

For Merit:
- One error.

For Excellence:
- I = 0.00337 kg m^2.

questions.text: Explain what will happen to the final velocity of the ball if the flywheel is replaced with a solid disc of the same radius and mass.
questions.expectedAnswer: A solid disc has mass distributed closer to the axis of rotation, so I decreases (I_disc = 1/2 mr^2 vs flywheel with mass at rim). Lower I means greater angular acceleration (tau = I alpha), so the ball falls faster and reaches a higher final velocity.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- I decreases.

For Merit:
- Links I to alpha.

For Excellence:
- Full explanation.

questions.text:
QUESTION THREE: SIMPLE HARMONIC MOTION

A marble is released on a watch glass and rolls back and forth with simple harmonic motion. The watch glass has a radius of curvature R.

State the two conditions necessary for simple harmonic motion.
questions.expectedAnswer: 1. The restoring force/acceleration is proportional to the displacement from equilibrium. 2. The restoring force/acceleration is always directed toward the equilibrium position.

questions.text:
The marble is released 0.0350 m from the right of equilibrium, and oscillates with a period of 0.950 s.

Using reference circles or otherwise, calculate the displacement of the marble after 1.30 seconds.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- omega correct.

For Merit:
- Minor mistake.

For Excellence:
- x = -0.0237 m (accept values between -0.023 m and -0.024 m).

questions.text:
Eventually, the marble comes to rest.

Draw a labelled graph of displacement vs time for five complete oscillations. Include values for displacement and time.
questions.expectedAnswer: Graph showing exponential decay envelope on a sinusoidal curve, starting at max amplitude 0.0350 m. Period remains constant at 0.950 s. Amplitude decreases each cycle.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Exponential decay shown. Period constant. Starts at max A.

questions.text:
Name this phenomenon, and explain in detail why the marble eventually comes to rest.

Support your answer with any relevant formulae.
questions.expectedAnswer: Damping. Friction between the marble and the glass converts kinetic energy to thermal energy. Each oscillation, the total energy decreases, so the maximum displacement (amplitude) decreases. Eventually all energy is lost and the marble stops. E_k = 1/2 mv^2, E_p = mgh.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Damping or friction or amplitude decreases.

For Merit:
- Damping AND energy loss.

For Excellence:
- Full explanation.
